metadata.title: Multi-Repo Codebase Investigation
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Systematic investigation of multiple repositories to answer a specific research question. Orchestrates per-repository investigation subprocesses with on-demand cloning (for remote repos) and automatic cleanup. Aggregates and synthesizes cross-repository findings into a comprehensive comparative report. Use when investigating patterns, implementations, or practices across multiple codebases.

researchQuestion.description: The specific question or investigation goal to answer across repositories
researchQuestion.example: How is authentication implemented across our microservices?

repositories.description: List of repository URLs or local paths to investigate (comma-separated). Supports GitHub URLs, other git hosting URLs, and local file system paths.

investigationScope.description: Specific areas or patterns to focus on within each repository. Narrows the investigation to relevant subsystems or concerns.

filePatterns.description: File patterns to search within each repository. Used to target specific file types or locations.

excludePatterns.description: Patterns to exclude from investigation. Used to skip irrelevant directories such as build outputs or third-party code.

outputFormat.description: Desired output format for the final investigation report.

steps.name: Understand Investigation Context
steps.output: Context documentation with research question, repositories list, and investigation scope
steps.context: Gathers and clarifies all parameters for the investigation. Produces a context document that defines the research question, lists all target repositories, and establishes the investigation scope. User approval confirms the context before investigation begins.

steps.name: Parse Repository List
steps.output: repositories-list.json with each repository entry containing: name, source, type (remote/local), subProcessId (null), subProcessPath (null), status (pending)
steps.context: Lightweight parsing step. Reads the comma-separated repositories parameter and produces a structured JSON file. Determines if each entry is a remote URL or local path. Does NOT clone any repositories — that is handled by each subprocess in Step 3.

steps.name: Investigate Repositories (Subprocess Loop)
steps.output: Spawned subprocesses for each repository; repositories-list.json updated with subProcessId, subProcessPath, and status for each entry
steps.context: Spawns one investigate-single-repo subprocess per repository. Passes researchQuestion, investigationScope, filePatterns, and excludePatterns to each subprocess. Updates repositories-list.json with subprocess tracking data. Does NOT wait for subprocesses to complete here — continues to Step 4 which is the sync point.

subProcessParameters.repositorySource: URL or local path from repositories-list.json entry
subProcessParameters.repositoryName: Repository name extracted from URL or path

steps.name: Aggregate and Synthesize Findings
steps.output: comparative-analysis.md with common patterns, differences, unique implementations, anomalies, and cross-cutting recommendations
steps.context: SYNC POINT: Waits for all subprocesses from Step 3 to complete. Reads repositories-list.json to locate each subprocess and its findings. Reads summary.json and repo-findings.md from each subprocess. Aggregates relevance determinations and findings. Performs cross-repository comparison: identifies common patterns, highlights differences, detects anomalies. Produces comparative-analysis.md for user approval.

steps.name: Create Investigation Report
steps.output: investigation-report.md (or .json based on outputFormat) with executive summary, per-repository findings, comparative analysis, recommendations, and conclusion
steps.context: Structures the final report based on the outputFormat parameter. Draws from comparative-analysis.md (Step 4) and per-repository findings. Sections include: Executive Summary, Research Question, Repositories Investigated (total/relevant/not-relevant counts), Per-Repository Findings, Comparative Analysis, Common Patterns, Unique Approaches, Recommendations, Conclusion.

steps.name: Continuous Improvement
steps.output: Improvements implemented to template, step definitions, or process

steps.name: End Process Validation
steps.output: Compliance report confirming all steps completed, all artifacts present, and process files valid

architecture.description: This template uses a parent-subprocess architecture. The parent process handles orchestration and aggregation. Each repository is investigated by a dedicated subprocess.
parentResponsibilities: Parse repository list into structured format
Wait for all subprocesses at Step 4 sync point
subprocessResponsibilities: Clone repository if remote (to temp directory)
Check repository relevance to research question
Delete cloned repository (if it was cloned)

keyBehaviors: On-demand cloning: repositories are only cloned when their subprocess begins, not in advance
Automatic cleanup: each subprocess deletes its cloned repository after investigation
Local path preservation: local repositories are never deleted
Subprocess isolation: a clone or investigation failure in one subprocess does not block others
Tracking in file: all subprocess tracking data lives in repositories-list.json, not parent memory

repositoryListJson.description: Central tracking file created in Step 2, updated in Step 3, and read in Step 4

schema.name: string - repository name extracted from URL or path
schema.source: string - original URL or local path
schema.subProcessId: string | null - UUID of spawned subprocess, populated in Step 3
schema.subProcessPath: string | null - filesystem path to subprocess directory, populated in Step 3

subProcessOutputs.description: Each investigate-single-repo subprocess produces these artifacts in its process directory
files: repo-findings.md - Detailed findings (only if repository is relevant)
summary.json - Structured output for parent: { repositoryName, relevance, findingsSummary, outputFiles }

memoryFileUsage.description: Configuration for how memory.json is used during this process
parentMemoryTracks: Count of relevant vs not-relevant repositories
memoryFileUsage.note: Subprocess tracking data is intentionally kept in repositories-list.json rather than parent memory.json for better data locality and easier access by Step 4 aggregation.
